source.title: Ellipsoid Control: A White-List Jailbreak Defense via Benign Latent Modeling
source.authors: Luo-Yu Chen; Wei-Qi Wang; Zhi-Yi Tian; Feng Wu; Ahmed Asiri; Shui Yu

record.tranche_reason: The authors report that Ellipsoid Control produces diverse drift directions across samples and argue these are difficult to represent with one vector. This is a refinement relevant to V4, but it measures EC's input-specific updates rather than the model's naturally encoded refusal direction.
record.gate_note: The paper uses refusal-likelihood optimization under a benign-data-derived ellipsoid, not the difference-in-means direction or its ablation/addition. Its main ASR and utility results evaluate EC's defense, not the single-direction claim, so they are not rows for those versions. The cited refusal-direction methods and their reported results are background only.
record.test_reason: This is a jailbreak-defense paper. It borrows the original paper's layer-selection criterion (Appendix A) to choose where Ellipsoid Control injects its per-input drift. It reports only EC's own ASR, utility and over-refusal against baselines. It never computes a difference-in-means direction, ablates or adds one, or measures the model's own refusal representation. The 'diverse drift directions' remark in Section IV-F (Fig. 5) describes EC's optimized updates, not how refusal is encoded in the model. That is a different construct, so it cannot bear on V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that Ellipsoid Control is a white-list, test-time defense: per-input PGD toward a refusal phrase, constrained by an anisotropic ellipsoid fitted to benign hidden states. They report that it lowers jailbreak ASR, including against SoftPrompt, while keeping MMLU and MT-Bench close to the undefended models and over-refusal lower than the baselines. They use the diverse drift directions and the LoRA-Steer ablation to argue for per-input optimization over a universal linear transformation. They make no claim about the structure of the model's refusal representation.
record.recipe_differences: Optimizes a refusal-phrase likelihood for each inspected input using projected gradient steps constrained by an ellipsoid fitted to benign hidden states; it does not use a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported drift magnitudes vary by input type: GPTFuzz and AutoDAN receive large shifts, while PAIR and SoftPrompt receive smaller shifts; benign and boundary inputs are reported to shift little.

fits_no_version.finding: On Llama-3-8B, the drift EC applies to jailbreak inputs points in diverse directions, both within and across attack methods. This is shown only qualitatively in t-SNE plots. A single learned low-rank transform (LoRA-Steer) defends worse than per-input optimization (Table I).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-eliciting activation interventions that are optimized per input under a benign-geometry constraint vary in direction across jailbreak inputs, and outperform a single shared transformation for defense.

record.problems: The directional-diversity evidence is qualitative and does not quantify direction similarity or directly test the natural refusal representation. The study does not compare EC's updates with the original difference-in-means direction.
record.rows_left_out: The paper's ASR, benign-task, and over-refusal table results, as well as its LoRA-Steer and PGD-Sphere comparisons, evaluate EC and alternative defenses rather than the refusal-direction versions in the claim. Figure-only drift magnitudes and other analyses likewise do not directly measure V4's underlying refusal representation.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction is computed, ablated or added. Only the original paper's layer-selection criterion is reused.
Does not test whether jailbreaks suppress the refusal direction. No training against ablation.
Does not characterize the model's natural refusal representation as affine, a cone, or multi-directional. The drift diversity concerns EC's optimized updates only.
Harm judgment is not separated from the refusal decision.
No transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
No analysis of how refusal training affects the direction.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T5' with V4 'supports' is not justified. The only link to the original paper is reuse of its layer-selection procedure, plus Jailbreak Antidote (which uses a refusal vector) as a baseline. Jailbreak Antidote's ASR numbers are a baseline comparison, not a test of V1 or V3.

versions.untested_parts: Does not identify a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, ablate it across layers and positions, or test adding it.
Does not turn ablation into a weight edit or test abliteration in released models.
Does not test whether attacks suppress the claimed direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
Does not test whether the model's natural refusal representation is affine, a cone, or a dominant direction plus others; the reported directional diversity concerns EC's optimized updates.
Does not separate harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
Does not test transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
Does not test how refusal training determines whether one removable direction exists.

rows.subject: L LAMA 3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Observed directions of EC's input-specific refusal-elicitation drift

conditions.value: jailbreak samples, within and across attack methods

rows.measure: Diversity of drift directions across samples
rows.value: The authors report diverse drift directions both among samples from the same jailbreak method and across methods, and say this is difficult to represent with a single vector.
rows.note: The explicit qualitative statement concerns EC-generated updates, not a direct measurement of the model's underlying refusal representation.
rows.check: The row measures how diverse EC's optimized per-input drift directions are, read qualitatively from t-SNE plots. It does not measure whether the model's refusal is mediated by one direction or several. Directions chosen by a likelihood optimizer under an ellipsoid constraint can vary across inputs even if refusal is one-dimensional. t-SNE also does not preserve directions, and no similarity metric or comparison with the difference-in-means direction is given.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: EC-generated updates on Llama 3-8B jailbreak samples
reader_labels.reason: Reported diversity of drift directions across samples and attack methods is consistent with the claim's multiple-directions aspect; this evidence is limited to EC updates (r1).
